items.title: Section: "By This, In This, For This" — Retracing How Undefiled, Tireless, Ever-Growing Practice Leads to Awakening

items.zh: 既發心已，方正修行自他利行。於自他利正修行時，得無雜染方便。無雜染故，得無厭倦方便。無厭倦故，得諸善根增長方便。於諸善根得增長已，能證無上正等菩提。又於如是自他利加行無雜染方便、無厭倦方便、善根增長方便，得大菩提中。將修行時，先於甚深廣大正法安立信解。立信解已，訪求正法。求正法已，廣為他說。亦於正行自能成辦。於成辦時，若由此、於此、為此應行。即由此、於此、為此而行。由此、於此、為此行時，如令福德、智慧增長所應行者，即如是行。福德、智慧既增長已，於不捨離生死方便能正修行。
items.en:
Second, effort-in-practice-holding; first, what is to be learned. Having aroused this aspiration, one then rightly practices for the benefit of self and others; in rightly practising, one attains undefiled skilful means; being undefiled, one attains tireless skilful means; being tireless, one attains the skilful means of growing wholesome roots; wholesome roots having grown, one can realise unsurpassed, perfect awakening.
Second, learning in this way. In cultivating these skilful means — undefiled, tireless, and growing in wholesome roots — towards great awakening, one first establishes faith and understanding in the profound, vast true dharma; having established this, one seeks out the true dharma; having sought it, one widely teaches it to others while also accomplishing correct practice oneself. In accomplishing this, one acts by this, in this, and for this, exactly as is fitting.
Third, being able to learn; first, the six perfections, four means of attraction, and offerings to the three jewels. Acting by this, in this, and for this, one acts exactly as fitting to grow merit and wisdom. Merit and wisdom having grown, one rightly practises the skilful means of never abandoning saṃsāra.

items.title: Section: Fourteen Qualities of a Bodhisattva's Practice, Retracing the Chapter on Factors of Awakening

items.zh: 即於此中正修行時，能行生死無雜染行。即於此中正修行時，能於自樂行無著行。即於此中正修行時，能於無量生死大苦能正修行無厭倦行。由於生死無厭倦故，能正訪求種種異論，於一切論得無所畏。善知論已，復能了知所應為說、所可宣說、應如是說，由此智故善知世間。如是菩薩善知諸論及世間已，復能如理訪求正法。既訪求已，堪能善斷一切有情一切疑惑。如是堪能斷他疑惑，令自福德展轉增長，福德資糧漸得圓滿；令自智慧亦轉增長，智慧資糧漸得圓滿。二種資糧既圓滿已，於諦行相、菩提分法無倒修中，能勤修行。於修方便能正了知。即持如是正勤所修，迴向大乘般涅槃果，不求聲聞及獨覺乘般涅槃果。既得如是方便善巧，能於一切菩薩語言聽聞受持。依修力故，於昔未聞所有諸法一切種相皆能辨了，於陀羅尼無礙辯才皆得圓滿。為欲永斷一切障故，精勤修習三解脫門。即於此中正修行時，為斷自他一切顛倒增上慢故，勤修正行，如是能於一切種相正行圓滿。
items.en:
Second, the factors of awakening; first, conscience and shame. In rightly practising amid this, one practices free of the defilement of saṃsāra.
Second, firm, resolute steadfastness. In rightly practising, one practices one's own joy without attachment.
Third, a mind never wearied. In rightly practising, one practices, amid the immeasurable great suffering of saṃsāra, without weariness.
Fourth, skilful mastery of every treatise. Being untiring amid saṃsāra, one rightly seeks out every manner of doctrine, attaining fearlessness regarding every treatise.
Fifth, skilful understanding of the world. Having mastered the treatises, one further comes to know what should be taught, what may be proclaimed, and how it should be expressed; by this wisdom, one skilfully understands the world.
Sixth, cultivating the correct four reliances. Having thus mastered the treatises and the world, one further rightly seeks out the true dharma.
Seventh, cultivating unimpeded understanding. Having sought it out, one becomes capable of resolving every doubt of every being.
Eighth, the provisions for awakening. Being capable of resolving others' doubts, one's own merit grows ever more complete, and one's own wisdom likewise grows ever more complete.
Ninth, cultivating the factors of awakening. Both provisions having become complete, one diligently practises the aspects of the truths and the factors of awakening without distortion.
Tenth, cultivating calm and insight. One rightly understands the skilful means of cultivation.
Eleventh, skilful means. Holding to this diligent cultivation, one dedicates it to the Great Vehicle's own nirvāṇa, not seeking the śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha's own nirvāṇa.
Twelfth, wondrous dhāraṇī. Having attained such skilful means, one can hear and uphold every bodhisattva teaching; by the power of cultivation, one comes to understand even what was never before heard, perfecting unimpeded eloquence through dhāraṇī.
Thirteenth, the three concentrations. Wishing to permanently sever every obstruction, one diligently cultivates the three gates of liberation.
Fourteenth, the four summarising verses of dharma. In rightly practising, in order to sever every distorted view and over-estimation in oneself and others, one diligently cultivates correct practice, thereby perfecting practice in every respect.

items.title: Section: A Bodhisattva's Own Virtues Retraced — Surpassing Every Being, Even the Two Lesser Vehicles

items.zh: 如是正行得圓滿已，於一切有情及聲聞、獨覺皆為殊勝。所謂正行功德殊勝。及可稱讚功德殊勝。
items.en: Third, a bodhisattva's own virtues; first, stating. Correct practice having thus reached completion, one surpasses every being, including śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas — namely, in the excellence of correct practice, and the excellence of praiseworthy qualities.

items.title: Section: Rare Yet Ordinary, Predicted and Never Retrogressing — The Bodhisattva Virtues Chapter Continues

items.zh: 當知此中，正行功德殊勝菩薩，為利自他勤修正行，用利他事以為自事，聲聞、獨覺則不如是。由諸菩薩用利他事為自事故，於一切有情起如自己平等之心。由起如是平等心故，於諸有情常施恩惠。不望其報。菩薩如是勤修行時，常於有情發起希望，欲令彼得利益安樂。由是利益安樂意樂，常能起作不虛加行。當知是名展轉引發正行功德殊勝。當知此中，稱讚功德殊勝菩薩，於諸佛所獲得授記，非諸聲聞，亦非獨覺。得授記已，便能安住不退轉地。安住此中，能於一切決定所作、恒常所作，獲得堅固無忘失法。如是堅固無忘失法，諸佛菩薩施設，在於一切有情最上施設。普於一切所應作事能無退失。於未得退亦無退失。無退失時，恒常無間，一切善法運運增長，如明分月。由諸善法轉增長故，菩薩爾時得名真實，不名相似。由得真實菩薩名故，於一切種一切有情調伏方便，如實了知。
items.en:
First, rare and not rare. Know that the bodhisattva of excellent correct practice, diligently practising to benefit self and others, treats benefiting others as benefiting himself; śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas are not so.
Second, equal-minded benevolence. Because bodhisattvas treat benefiting others as benefiting themselves, they arouse an equal mind towards all beings as towards themselves; by this equal mind, they constantly bestow kindness without expecting reward.
Third, effort never wasted. Practising diligently thus, bodhisattvas constantly wish beings to attain benefit and ease; by this intention, their effort is never wasted.
Second, excellent praiseworthy qualities; first, distinguishing; first, receiving prediction and the rest; first, receiving the Buddha's prediction. Know that the bodhisattva of excellent praiseworthy quality receives prediction from the buddhas, which neither śrāvakas nor pratyekabuddhas receive.
Second, settling into certainty. Having received prediction, one settles securely into the stage of non-retrogression.
Third, deeds certain and constant. Abiding there, one attains firm, unforgetting dharma regarding every decisively necessary and constantly necessary deed.
Fourth, the supreme designation. Such firm, unforgetting dharma makes the buddhas' and bodhisattvas' own designation the most supreme designation among all beings.
Second, freedom from distortion and the rest; first, effort without retrogression. Universally, with respect to every task to be done, there is no retrogression, nor any retrogression regarding what is not yet attained.
Second, progressive growth. Without retrogression, constantly and without interruption, every wholesome dharma grows, like the waxing moon.
Third, named genuine, not merely resembling. Because wholesome dharmas thus grow, the bodhisattva then earns the name genuine, not merely resembling.
Fourth, skilfully knowing how to tame. Having earned the name genuine bodhisattva, one truly knows every skilful means for taming every kind of being.

blocks.text: The retrospective continues, recalling the chapters on the factors of awakening and on a bodhisattva's qualities.

subs.head: By this, in this, for this

blocks.text: Both lecturers: the prajñā of non-attainment is the "undefiled means". Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva cycles in saṃsāra for beings, yet does not stay there in vain, accomplishing great benefit.
Venerable Miào Jìng: the concentration named here is the samādhi of suchness.
Excellence of correct practice and of praiseworthy qualities.

Venerable Miào Jìng: benefiting beings is benefiting oneself; would one expect oneself to repay? Master Cháng Bǎi: self-benefit is completed through benefiting others. One settles into non-retrogression; Venerable Miào Jìng, one who has not seen the ultimate may still regress.
"Would one expect oneself to repay?" Venerable Miào Jìng's question undoes the whole idea of a favour owed.

quiz.q: What is "undefiled skilful means," per the lectures?
quiz.why: Both: the prajñā of non-attainment is the undefiled means.

quiz.q: "Never abandoning saṃsāra." How do the lectures explain the bodhisattva's being there?
options: not staying in vain, accomplishing great benefit for self and beings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva cycles for beings yet doesn't stay there in vain, accomplishing great benefit. Venerable Miào Jìng agrees.

quiz.q: "Practices one's own joy without attachment." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say the "own joy" is?
options: the samādhi of suchness; even this bliss isn't clung to
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: it is the samādhi of suchness. The English does not specify this.

quiz.q: In which two excellences does the bodhisattva surpass all?
quiz.why: Excellence of correct practice and of praiseworthy qualities.

quiz.q: "Bestowing kindness without expecting reward." What reason does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: benefiting beings is benefiting oneself — would one expect repayment from oneself?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: benefiting beings is benefiting oneself; would one expect oneself to repay? Master Cháng Bǎi: self-benefit is completed through benefiting others.

quiz.q: What follows the bodhisattva's receiving prediction?
quiz.why: One settles into non-retrogression. Venerable Miào Jìng: one who hasn't seen the ultimate may still regress.
